messages:
sre-alex: Heads up — getting a flurry of 503s for a hosted tenant (acme). Looks like upstream inference workers are exiting. Dumping initial error: `SIGSEGV` then `GPU OOM` in same hour. Anyone oncall?
eng-jin: oncall-lee is live, pinged. Do we have a reproducible request pattern?
support-maria: Customer report: large toolcall + long context. They say it started ~10:02 UTC, ~p95 latency then 503s. CS Jim copied logs.
cs-jim: their payloads include a 120k token input + chained toolcalls, but average before was 30k. They replayed one failing request and got 503 consistently.
oncall-lee: I'm on. Attached recent runner logs from that pod. Noticing repeated: `nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo` spikes then `cudaMalloc` fail.
eng-jin: paste logs?
oncall-lee: ```
[2025-06-12T10:03:21Z] runner-7f4b SIGSEGV at 0x7f...
[2025-06-12T10:03:22Z] runtime: attempt kv-prefetch size=1.2GB
[2025-06-12T10:03:22Z] cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2025-06-12T10:03:23Z] worker exiting code=139
```
sre-alex: Interesting — segfault right after a large prefetch + cudaMalloc OOM. Could be a memory accounting race when KV prefetch spikes. Any recent change to prefetch heuristics?
eng-jin: No config rollouts today. We did a small quant swap for a model last night but it was applied to a different pool. I'll check kernel traces.
support-maria: Customer also reported intermittent auth 401s earlier but that looks separate. This is definitely runtime worker crash causing 503s.
eng-jin: Repro plan: ask CS to replay failing request with env `REDWOOD_PREFETCH=0` to disable prefetch, see if it avoids OOM/segfault. If that helps we have a quick mitigation.
cs-jim: I'm asking them now. They can toggle headers on replay.
oncall-lee: In parallel, I'm scaling the pool down/up for that tenant to force warm restarts and collect heap profile.
sre-alex: Also capture `nvidia-smi` timeline during repro — want memory graphs. Could be fragmentation plus large dynbatch.
eng-jin: If disabling prefetch fixes it, we'll revert the heuristic change in the runtime and add a guard to avoid prefetched chunk > 50% free GPU mem.
support-maria: Customer replies: after replay with `REDWOOD_PREFETCH=0` - request succeeded, no 503. They ran 10 attempts.
oncall-lee: Good signal. I'm going to promote a temporary routing rule to route this tenant to a different pool with stricter mem caps.
sre-alex: Can we make a fast rollback patch to add a guard and ship to canary? If not, apply config guard server-side ASAP.
eng-jin: I have a 1-line patch to check free mem before prefetch. Will open PR and push to canary in 10m.
support-maria: Escalation note: customer impact for ~40m, CS informed, billing hold requested for window.
cs-jim: Filed a billing request, attaching incident ID 2025-INC-4872.
oncall-lee: Afterrouting change, 0 503s for that tenant in the last 5m. Collecting postmortem artifacts (core dump, heap) now.
sre-alex: Thanks everyone. Next steps: (1) eng-jin push prefetch guard to canary, (2) oncall collect and upload heap/core, (3) support coordinate customer compensation. I'll create the postmortem stub.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary pool update (prefetch-guard) by eng-jin at 2025-06-12T10:28:03Z
eng-jin: Can confirm canary saw same long replay with prefetch enabled -> OOM -> failure; with guard enabled -> passes. Preparing rollback and long-term fix plan to avoid segfault on OOM.
support-maria: Noted for CS: customer wants a follow-up call. I'll coordinate.
sre-alex: Filing ticket for follow-up: add better mem accounting, add config circuit-breaker for prefetch, add telemetry to surface large prefetch attempts per-tenant.
eng-jin: I'll own the follow-up. Will include repro steps and a small stress test harness to replay huge toolcalls safely.
sre-alex: Great. Closing Slack thread when postmortem is up. :thumbsup:
